Washington County by the numbers

What is Washington County, Arkansas, and who lives there?

Washington County is in the Ozark Mountains of northwest Arkansas, with Fayetteville as both its county seat and largest city. It covers 951.72 square miles, which makes it the fourth-largest Arkansas county by area, and its population was 245,871 in the 2020 census with a 2025 estimate of 271,213. Only two other Arkansas counties have more people.

Thirteen incorporated places lie in the county: Elkins, Elm Springs, Farmington, Fayetteville, Goshen, Greenland, Johnson, Lincoln, Prairie Grove, Springdale, Tontitown, West Fork and Winslow. Elm Springs and Springdale extend into Benton County. If your house is in one of those two cities, check which county's assessor and collector bill the parcel before you contact anyone.

The northern and western parts are rolling Springfield Plateau, while the south is steeper, forested Boston Mountains. The county neighbors Benton County to the north, Madison County to the east, Crawford County to the south and Adair County, Oklahoma to the west. Interstate 49 is the main thoroughfare, linking the University of Arkansas with Fort Smith and Interstate 40.

What drives the economy and housing demand in Washington County?

The county's economy rests on business and management, education, sales, office work and poultry production. The University of Arkansas, founded in Fayetteville in 1871 as Arkansas Industrial University, is the state's largest institution of higher learning, with 23,025 undergraduates in fall 2019. Apples were the economic base in the late 19th century.

Springdale Public Schools reports more than 23,000 students and is described as the state's largest district, and its employers include Tyson Foods, which has its world headquarters in Springdale.

The ground itself can affect value. Karst features such as springs, sinkholes and caves are common in the county, and the Encyclopedia of Arkansas says solution and collapse sinkholes are abundant in the Boone Formation limestone of the Springfield Plateau. Sellers with a sinkhole or settling foundation should expect buyers to ask about it.

Which Washington County offices handle property tax?

Three county offices split the work: the Assessor values property, the County Clerk runs the Equalization Board appointments, and the Collector sends bills and takes payment. The Treasurer is a separate office that the Collector page lists as related.

OfficeWhat it doesContact on the official pages
AssessorValues real and personal property, hears informal appealsAppraiser, 479-444-1500, weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.
County ClerkSchedules Equalization Board hearings479-444-1711
CollectorMails statements, collects tax479-444-1526 if no statement by April 15

The Assessor's site offers a free property search. The Collector's site has a Search Tax Records option for receipts. Online payment is by credit card only and includes a processing fee, and you can also pay by mail or in person.

How does Washington County assess a house?

Washington County values real estate at market value, meaning the likely sale price in an arm's-length sale, except for bona fide farmland, which is valued by use. The Assessor uses mass appraisal, grouping homes into neighborhoods with similar characteristics. Under Act 139 of 2023, counties must reappraise market-value real estate every four years, and this county's cycle began in 2023.

New construction is added every year. Owners should report it, and permitted construction inside cities is followed by field inspections. If you build a garage, finish a basement or add a room before selling, expect the value to change on the next assessment.

The site does not state the assessment ratio or the millage rate. It says tax rates are set yearly by the school districts and the elected county and city officials, and the Collector page says the bill is about 1 percent of the value of your home, car and other property. Use the figure as a rough guide only.

What reductions apply to a primary residence in Washington County?

The homestead credit lowers the bill by up to $600 on the owner's primary residence. Owners must tell the Assessor in the county where they live to claim it.

  • Taxable value increases caused by reappraisal are capped at 5 percent a year on a primary residence, and 10 percent on vacant and commercial property.
  • Owners 65 or older, or disabled under Social Security standards, have a taxable value that cannot rise because of reappraisal.
  • Seniors and disabled owners provide a driver's license or state ID, or proof of disability.
  • The provisions apply even if the home is in a trust or the occupant lives in a nursing home.
  • Mobile and modular homes are assessed as real estate and are eligible.

Owners claim the credit with the Assessor, so a buyer who will live in the house should contact that office after closing.

When are Washington County property taxes due, and what happens if they are late?

Real estate and personal property taxes are due October 15, and property is assessed between January 1 and May 31. Arkansas bills in arrears, so the bill you pay in October of one year reflects an assessment made earlier.

Real estate paid after October 15 carries a 10 percent penalty and 10 percent annual interest. Personal property paid late takes the 10 percent penalty. Personal property assessed after May 31 adds a 10 percent late assessment fee, and newly purchased property can be assessed within 30 days of purchase without that penalty. The Texarkana Gazette reported, for Miller County, that unpaid real estate taxes may be sent to the Commissioner of State Lands for collection, so ask the Collector how that works here.

When a sale closes in the middle of a year, ask the title company how it will handle a tax bill that has not been issued yet. Settle that in the contract so the buyer and seller both know who owes what.

How do you appeal a Washington County assessment?

Start by calling the appraiser at 479-444-1500 on or before the third Monday in August, then book an Equalization Board hearing through the County Clerk if the issue is not fixed. The board sits from August 1 through September 30, and appointments must be made on or before the third Monday in August. A decision can go on to County Court and then Circuit Court.

The 2026 calendar shows how tight the window is:

  • July: the Assessor sends notices.
  • July 13: the Clerk begins scheduling appointments.
  • August 1: the board holds its first meeting.
  • August 17: the last day to schedule a hearing.
  • September 30: last day for regular meetings.
  • October 12: last day to appeal to County Court.
  • November 20: end of any special session, and the last date an assessment may change.

Bring comparable sales, repair estimates and photos of the problem. If the house is under contract, the appeal can wait only as long as the dates above allow.

What does it cost to transfer a Washington County house?

The Arkansas real property transfer tax is $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration on a deed, so $330 on a $100,000 sale. The Department of Finance and Administration's page does not say which side pays, so agree it in the contract. It sells transfer stamps through its Miscellaneous Tax Section, which can be reached at 501-682-7187.

When does a cash sale help a Washington County owner with tax due?

A cash sale can help when back taxes, repairs or a tenant make a regular listing hard. Cash Home Buyers purchases houses as-is, and we explain what the title company will pay from your proceeds before you decide. We do not promise a price before we review the property.

October 15 each year. After that date, real estate takes a 10 percent penalty plus 10 percent annual interest.

How do I appeal my Washington County assessment?

Call the Assessor's appraiser at 479-444-1500, then schedule an Equalization Board hearing through the County Clerk at 479-444-1711. Both must happen by the third Monday in August.

What is the homestead credit in Washington County?

It is a credit of up to $600 on your primary residence. You must notify the Assessor to claim it.

Is there a limit on how much my assessment can rise?

Yes. On a primary residence, reappraisal increases in taxable value are capped at 5 percent a year, and owners 65 or older or disabled have no reappraisal increase.

Who do I call if I did not get my tax statement?

Call the Collector at 479-444-1526 if the statement has not arrived by April 15.

Does Springdale pay Washington County or Benton County tax?

It depends on the parcel. Springdale lies in both counties, so check which county your property is in.

Where is Conway County, Arkansas?

Conway County lies in the Arkansas River Valley of central Arkansas, between the Ozark Mountains to the north and the Ouachita Mountains to the south. It is about 52 miles northwest of Little Rock and 109 miles east of Fort Smith, and at roughly 567 square miles it is the fifth smallest county in the state.

Neighbors are Faulkner County to the east, Perry to the south, Van Buren to the north, Yell to the southwest and Pope to the west. Morrilton is the county seat and largest city. Plumerville and Oppelo are incorporated towns, and Menifee appears in the township listings.

The county is one of the older ones. It was created on October 20, 1825, as Arkansas's 11th county, from part of Pulaski County, and named for territorial delegate Henry Wharton Conway. Van Buren, Perry and Faulkner counties were later carved out of its original territory.

How did Morrilton become the county seat?

Morrilton took the seat from Lewisburg after the railroad arrived. Lewisburg served as county seat from 1831 to 1883, but a depot planned in 1871 on land sold by farmer E. J. Morrill drew residents away, and county government moved in 1883.

Morrilton had 6,992 residents in the 2020 census, with a 2025 estimate of 7,195. Interstate 40 runs along the north side of the city, US 64 is the main road through downtown, and Arkansas Highways 9 and 95 also serve it. The Arkansas River forms the southern edge of the city, and Morrilton Municipal Airport is the local airfield. Most county offices, including the courts and the assessor, are in Morrilton.

Two other facts help place the county. Petit Jean State Park, Arkansas's oldest state park, covers 3,471 acres near Morrilton, and the 2010 center of population of the whole state was in Conway County, near Plumerville.

What are the main employers in Conway County?

Manufacturing is the headline. Green Bay Packaging announced on June 3, 2025, a project of more than $1 billion at its Morrilton mill, which makes linerboard for corrugated packaging. The company has more than 620 employees in the county, the project adds 35 jobs, and the expansion could more than double the mill's production capacity.

The project also moved roads. Six counties, one city and the Arkansas Department of Transportation relocated Highway 113 in 2024 to make room. The company plans to buy about 300 acres for future growth.

The University of Arkansas Community College at Morrilton and the South Conway County School District are the other anchors in town. The district operates the public schools, with Morrilton High School as its high school.

Which offices handle property tax in Conway County?

The assessor and the collector share the same address, 117 S. Moose Street in Morrilton, AR 72110. Assessor Mark Stobaugh keeps office hours Monday through Friday from 8:00 to 4:30 and can be reached at (501) 354-9622. State law, section 26-26-715, requires the assessor to maintain current appraisal and assessment records, which includes updating values when land use or improvements change.

The county collector, Norbert Gunderman, collects the property taxes for the county, its municipalities, the public schools, the library and improvement districts. Both offices link to the actDataScout vendor for tax and real estate record searches.

The collector's page we read did not list a phone number, due dates, penalties or payment methods, so confirm those directly. Other Arkansas county collectors, including Baxter and Benton, use an October 15 deadline with a 10 percent penalty after it.

How do you appeal a Conway County valuation?

You apply to the county equalization board on or before the third Monday in August. Section 26-27-317 says the board must begin hearing appeals no later than the second Monday in August, and an owner may appear in person or send written documentation.

  • The board must decide and notify you in writing at least ten business days after the hearing.
  • The notice must state the right to appeal to county court and the deadline for that petition.
  • Evidence not given to the assessor at least five business days before the hearing may lead to a continuance.
  • A petition filed for a business entity must be signed and filed by an Arkansas-licensed attorney.

The Conway assessor's page did not describe a county appeal procedure or a reappraisal date, so ask the office which year Conway's next reappraisal falls in. Arkansas Business reported that annual increases are capped at 5 percent for a primary residence, 10 percent for commercial property, and that counties are moving to a four-year cycle.

What happens if Conway County taxes go unpaid?

Land with unpaid tax can eventually be certified to the Commissioner of State Lands, who must notify the owner and offer redemption. Section 26-37-301 lets the owner or another person with no ownership interest redeem by paying all taxes, penalties, interest and costs, including the cost of the notice.

  • The sale date must be at least one year after certification.
  • The notice goes by certified mail, then regular mail if the first is unclaimed or refused.
  • For a homestead without proof of receipt, personal service is required at least 60 days before the sale.

For a seller with a delinquent bill, early contact with the collector gives you a payoff figure and keeps options open.

What do sellers in Conway County usually face?

The numbers explain a lot. The county's population fell 2.6 percent between 2010 and 2020, and 13.1 percent of housing units were vacant in 2020. Vacant houses are one situation a seller here may be dealing with, and they come with their own upkeep and tax questions.

Climate matters for repairs. Morrilton has a humid subtropical climate with about 51.20 inches of precipitation a year and 2.4 inches of snow, so roofs, gutters and crawl spaces take steady moisture. The county also holds Petit Jean State Park, Cove Creek Natural Area and five wildlife management areas, which keeps part of the land out of development.

  • Houses sitting vacant after a death or a move.
  • Owners who cannot find the cash for roof, foundation or plumbing repairs.
  • Rental properties with a tenant who has left or stopped paying.
  • Back taxes tied to a probate that has not started.

Where do I pay Conway County property tax?

At the county collector's office at 117 S. Moose Street in Morrilton, AR 72110. The office also lists an online tax record search through actDataScout, but confirm payment methods and dates with the office.

What is the deadline to appeal a Conway County assessment?

The third Monday in August under Ark. Code 26-27-317. The application goes to the county equalization board, which must start hearing appeals by the second Monday in August.

How big is Conway County?

About 567 square miles, the fifth smallest county in Arkansas. It had 20,715 residents in the 2020 census.

Is Conway County the same as the city of Conway?

No. Conway County's seat is Morrilton. The city of Conway is in Faulkner County, which borders Conway County to the east.

Can I sell a house in Conway County with back taxes?

Nothing we read bars it. Ask the collector for the amount owed, including penalty, and settle it as part of the sale.
